releases.title: Discovery: one catalog to approve from

New: For the site owner: the Discovery page has an "All runs combined" catalog with every statistic from every finished run, and which runs each one came from. A character sampled by more than one run counts once, with its newest values. It also says which rulesets and factions the combined sample covers. This is the catalog to approve suggestions from, and it downloads as CSV.
"Re-analyse all runs" re-analyses every finished run with the current rules and rebuilds the combined catalog, using only the responses already stored. It asks Blizzard nothing.
A statistic's value type can be confirmed or corrected. The new "Guessed types" view lists every type that is still a guess. Your choice replaces the guess and survives later re-analyses.
Fixed: Two statistics with identical values are no longer treated as the same thing. "Professions learned" and "Professions at maximum skill" matched only because the sampled characters were low level. Equal values now produce a "possible duplicate" suggestion that shows its evidence: how many characters have both, and how many of those values are non-zero. It is a "likely" duplicate when the names say the same thing too. Nothing stops counting toward a tier as a duplicate until you approve the pairing, and both always keep their leaderboards.

Value types no longer read too much into a name. "Battlegrounds played" was taken for a length of time; it's a count. Time, gold and distance now need the name to state a unit or say so plainly, everything else defaults to a count, and anything that is still a guess says "guessed".

releases.title: Discovery: what the first run taught us

Improved: For the site owner: discovery now records each character's ruleset from its profile, and the Answers tab says how many sampled characters are on each ruleset, since tiers are graded within a ruleset.

Suggestions follow the grading decisions made after the first run. Every statistic gets a leaderboard, ties and name-plus-number ones included. Deaths, mishaps, duels lost and quests abandoned are leaderboard-only. Emotes, times camped and hearthing get their own category tier on the character page but never count toward the overall tier. When two statistics are exact duplicates, both keep a leaderboard and only one is graded.
Suggestions say what each statistic counts toward: its category and the overall tier, its category only, or no tier.

A Re-analyse button rebuilds a finished run's catalog, suggestions and answers with the current rules, from the responses it already stored. It asks Blizzard nothing, and decisions already made still apply.
Fixed: "Average quests completed per day" was taken for a duration; it's now recognised as a rate.
Statistics that come with a name beside their number (like "Creature type killed the most: Undead, 979") are now shown as name + number, ranked by the number.
"Duels lost" is now recognised as a bad statistic.
A discovery run no longer asks for the ruleset index twice: the index's link to itself was being followed as if it were a ruleset.

releases.title: Discovery: finding out what Blizzard's Forever API really returns

New: For the site owner: a Discovery page in the admin area. One button asks Blizzard's WoW Forever API about real characters: a primary character, every Forever character on the owner's Battle.net account, and the primary's guild roster, up to a cap (50 by default). It also asks for the rulesets, the guild's profile, roster, activity and achievements, and every character endpoint that might exist. Every answer is kept exactly as it came back, 404s and failures included, with how long it took and the headers Blizzard sent.

Discovery reads the owner's own characters with a Battle.net authorization asked for on the Discovery page. That token is stored encrypted, only discovery uses it, and it is deleted when Battle.net expires it (about a day). Signing in to Everstats works exactly as before.

Each run builds a catalog of every in-game statistic it saw: Blizzard's id, name and category, a guessed value type, and how many sampled characters have it. The catalog sorts, filters, and downloads as CSV or JSON.

Each statistic comes with three suggestions, each with its reason: which tier category it belongs in, whether it's a "bad" statistic like deaths (leaderboard only, never part of a tier), and whether it's worth a leaderboard at all. The owner approves or rejects them; a rejected one isn't suggested again. Nothing becomes a leaderboard or tier category from this yet.

The run answers the open questions directly: whether statistics exist for Forever's own systems (Camping, Legacy, Housing, Skyborne), how Blizzard addresses names with hyphens, spaces or capitals, whether the account listing is realm-based like retail's, how fresh the data is, whether character renders are available yet, and what rate-limit headers Blizzard sends.
Fixed: The home page said "US realms". Forever has no realms, so it now says "US region". So does the "character not found" message.

releases.title: The new look, and nightly backups

New: Everstats has its own look: "Cartographer's Ledger". A twilight map behind every page, character sheets in a gilt frame, shield-shaped tier badges, and Cinzel lettering for names and headings. Forever, Alliance and Horde are all redrawn; visitors still always see Forever.
The top bar has a character search on every page: type a name and surname (press / to jump to it). On a phone the bar folds into a search button and a menu.
A Guilds link in the top bar. Guild pages aren't built yet, and the page says so.

The database is backed up every night to a separate folder on the server. Each backup is read back in full before it's kept; the last 14 are kept, plus the first of every month for good. If one fails, the earlier ones stay and it tries again an hour later.

For the site owner: the admin page shows how backups are going (the last good one, its size, and why the last one failed if it did) and which addresses Cloudflare's tunnel connects from, to fill in TRUSTED_PROXIES.
Improved: Every page that isn't built yet says so in one clear "Coming soon" panel, and the other empty states stay easy to tell apart: "No data yet" is dashed, "No coverage here" is hatched, and "Unranked" shows the dash shield.

Opening a character now really asks the server and shows a loading sheet while it does, then says plainly that character pages are coming. If the server can't be reached, or you've looked up too many characters too quickly, it says that instead.

Settings: unlinking a sign-in, removing a passkey and turning two-factor off now ask you to confirm first. Recovery codes can be downloaded, copied or printed, and Finish waits until you tick that you've stored them. Choosing a theme confirms it's saved.
The two-factor step at sign-in has a "Use a recovery code instead" switch.
Merging accounts asks you to tick that you understand this account will be deleted before it goes ahead.
Fixed: The sign-in page no longer says sign-in "isn't set up yet" next to the passkey button. Passkeys are always offered. If your browser has no Everstats passkey, it now says: no passkey yet, sign in with Battle.net or Discord, then add one in Settings. "Not configured" is now shown only on a provider whose keys really aren't set.

The server now notes where Cloudflare's visitor-address header comes from on every page load, not only when someone signs in or does something else that's rate-limited, so the right TRUSTED_PROXIES value can be found.

releases.title: The foundations: a site you can open, sign in to, and theme

New: Everstats has a home page with a character search (name and surname). Lookups aren't switched on yet, so a search takes you to the character's page, which says plainly that there's no data for anyone yet.

Every page Everstats 1.0 will have is in place: character pages (hero, gear, core stats, statistics by category, tier letters, progress charts), leaderboards for each ruleset and category, single-statistic leaderboards and guild pages. Each says what it will show and that it's coming, with no sample numbers.

Accounts are optional. Sign in with Battle.net or Discord; the first sign-in makes your account. Until the site's keys are entered, the sign-in page says that sign-in isn't set up yet rather than offering a button that fails.

In Settings you can link a second provider, add passkeys (and then sign in with a passkey), turn on two-factor codes from an authenticator app with ten one-time recovery codes shown once, and merge a second account you made by mistake into the one you keep.

Three themes: Forever (twilight blue and gold), Alliance (royal blue, gold and parchment) and Horde (crimson, charcoal and bronze). Choosing a theme is for signed-in accounts and follows your account to every device; visitors always see Forever.
The version and a link to these notes sit in a bar at the bottom of every page.
